title: Cybersecurity Stocks Slide as AI Financing Jitters Spread: Palo Alto Falls 7%, SentinelOne Sinks 9%, Zscaler Drops 6%
source_used: 24/7 Wall St (read on Yahoo Finance copy)
key_facts: 24/7 Wall St, 16 Oct: in afternoon trading Palo Alto Networks fell 7% to $343.31, SentinelOne 9% to $21.29 and Zscaler 6% to $206.39.
The First Trust NASDAQ Cybersecurity ETF (CIBR) fell 4% against 1.72% for the Invesco QQQ Trust, which tracks the Nasdaq-100.
The stocks are pulling back from record highs set earlier this month.

On Thursday Citi raised its price target on Palo Alto and kept its Buy rating, citing a chief information officer survey showing improving security spending with AI deployments driving extra investment.
Palo Alto's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 34.5% to $3.41 billion; its fiscal 2027 outlook is $14.1 billion to $14.2 billion, growth of 23% to 24%.
Palo Alto sells firewalls and a security software platform, SentinelOne endpoint protection, and Zscaler cloud-delivered secure network access.
quote_evidence: Cybersecurity stocks are giving back ground as concerns about how AI spending gets funded spread across technology.
In afternoon trading, Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW) stock is down 7%, trading at $343.31.
Citi's analysts stated that the firm's chief information officer survey showed improving security spending, with AI deployments driving additional investment.
why_it_matters_hint: Even companies selling security for AI were sold with the rest of tech.
notes: Yahoo Finance copy of a 24/7 Wall St article (editorial@247wallst.com); promotional stock-pick text and the closing 'keep position sizes modest' line are not used (no investment advice). The article's aside about Palo Alto's chief executive 'at the time' is unclear and not used.
